group.title: Phrasal verbs
group.tagline: Give up, find out, carry on
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: To stop trying or stop doing something.
wrong: I gave up smoking, so I smoke more now.

words.meaning: To take care of someone or something.
examples: Can you {look after} my cat this weekend?
wrong: I looked after the plants, so they all died of thirst.

words.meaning: To try to find something.
wrong: I’m looking for my keys, which are in my hand.

words.meaning: To feel happy about something that is going to happen.
wrong: I look forward to the party because it happened last year.

words.meaning: To learn a fact or piece of information.
examples: I want to {find out} what time the shop opens.
wrong: I found out the answer, so I still don’t know it.

words.meaning: To arrive, often without warning.
examples: He {turned up} late to the meeting.
wrong: She turned up, so she never came.

words.meaning: To use all of something so there is none left.
wrong: We ran out of bread, so we have lots left.

words.meaning: To move something to a later time.
examples: Let’s {put off} the meeting until Friday.
wrong: We put off the trip, so we left a day early.

words.meaning: To start a business or organization.
wrong: He set up a shop by closing it.

words.meaning: To continue doing something.
wrong: Carry on means stop at once.

words.meaning: To leave the ground and start flying.
wrong: The plane took off and stayed on the ground.

words.meaning: To collect someone or something.
examples: I’ll {pick up} the kids from school at four.
wrong: I picked up the parcel, so it is still at the post office.

words.meaning: To return to a place.
wrong: He came back, so he never returned.

words.meaning: To feel better after an illness or a sad event.
examples: It took her months to {get over} the flu.
wrong: He got over his cold, so he is still sick.

words.meaning: To care for a child until it is an adult.
examples: She was {brought up} by her grandmother.
wrong: Her parents brought her up, so they never looked after her.

words.meaning: To decide that a planned event will not happen.
examples: They {called off} the match because of rain.
wrong: They called off the concert, so it went ahead as planned.

words.meaning: To write information in the spaces on a form.
wrong: I filled in the form by leaving it blank.

words.meaning: To give work to a teacher or person in charge.
wrong: I handed in my homework by keeping it at home.

words.meaning: To tell someone a fact they did not notice.
examples: She {pointed out} a mistake in my email.
wrong: He pointed out the error by hiding it.

words.meaning: To arrive at an event.
wrong: Nobody showed up, so the room was full.

words.meaning: To start a new hobby or activity.
wrong: She took up painting, so she stopped painting.

words.meaning: To do exercise to get fit.
examples: I {work out} at the gym every morning.
wrong: I work out by lying on the sofa all day.

words.meaning: To say no to an offer.
wrong: He turned down the offer, so he accepted it.

words.meaning: To leave home to do something for fun.
wrong: We went out, so we stayed at home all evening.

words.meaning: To find or meet something by chance.
examples: I {came across} an old photo in a drawer.
wrong: I came across the book after searching for months.

words.meaning: To take action to solve a problem.
wrong: She dealt with the problem by ignoring it.

words.meaning: To become slower.
wrong: He slowed down, so the car went faster.

words.meaning: To become happier, or make someone happier.
examples: A funny film helps me {cheer up}.
wrong: She cheered up, so she felt much sadder.

words.meaning: To become quiet and relaxed after being angry or excited.
examples: {Calm down} and tell me what happened.
wrong: Calm down means get angrier.

words.meaning: To get rid of something you do not want.
wrong: I threw away the box, so I kept it.

words.meaning: To start wearing clothes.
wrong: Put on your shoes means take them off.

words.meaning: To test something to see if it works.
wrong: We tried out the car by never driving it.

words.meaning: To go onto a bus, train or plane.
examples: We {got on} the bus at the station.
wrong: I got on the train, so I stayed on the platform.

words.meaning: To happen.
wrong: Nothing is going on, so a lot is happening.

words.meaning: To find information in a book or online.
examples: {Look up} the word in a dictionary.
wrong: I looked up the word by closing the dictionary.

words.meaning: To take someone to a place in a car and leave them there.
examples: Can you {drop off} the kids at school?
wrong: I dropped him off at the station, so he stayed in my car all day.

words.meaning: To look at something interesting.
wrong: I checked out the museum, so I never looked at it.

words.meaning: To return to a place.
examples: What time did you {get back} home?
wrong: We got back home, so we were still on holiday.

words.meaning: To stop working, used for machines and cars.
examples: Our car {broke down} on the highway.
wrong: The car broke down, so it worked perfectly.

words.meaning: To wait for a short time.
wrong: Hold on means hurry and leave now.
